raw_response:
I've farmed this same 10.7 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. At 65, with only primary schooling, I don't read manuals or chase new techniques — I watch the sky, feel the soil, and do what has always put food on the table for my five-person household. My well has never failed me, and the wheat-maize rotation is the backbone of our year.

This season, I will plant my **winter wheat** across the full 10.7 mu right after the autumn maize harvest. I'll rotary till the field first — the soil needs loosening after the maize stubble. I'll sow an improved wheat variety, the kind my neighbors and I have trusted for years. For fertilizer, I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting, then top-dress with urea at green-up — about 17 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, with 6 kg of phosphorus and 4 kg of potassium. I'll irrigate three times from my well: once before winter to help the seedlings establish, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading — three times is enough if you time them right. Two pesticide sprays will do, mainly for weeds and aphids. I expect about 480 kg per mu from the wheat; it's not the highest possible, but it's reliable.

When the wheat comes off in early June, I won't waste a day — summer heat waits for no one. I'll plant **summer maize** immediately on the same 10.7 mu with no-tillage sowing straight into the wheat stubble. At my age, saving a pass over the field saves my back and catches the season. I'll use hybrid seed — everyone around here does, and the vigor is worth it. I'll apply 16 kg nitrogen per mu, 5 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium. The maize will get two well irrigations: one around the jointing or tasseling stage, and one during grain filling if the summer rains are stingy. Two pesticide applications will keep the stem borers and leaf diseases in check. I expect roughly 520 kg per mu from the maize.

I don't over-fertilize or over-spray. I know that pushing for an extra 50 kg per mu can cost more in inputs than the grain is worth, and at my age, a stable harvest I can depend on beats a risky gamble every time.
